lanes.recommendation_note: PLR-077 is fixed by code reading: a Partial video receipt ends at the latest end of a picture handed to the sink, an empty span at the start when none was. The change is confined to Forward (one field, one helper, two lines after the sink call) and the Partial branch; choose(), the routing, the plane and size checks, the pump and every pre-existing error path are untouched. A fully delivered decode is unchanged (branch not entered), and a packet shortfall with every picture delivered yields the identical value. The test named fully_delivered_... contains a decoder-drop sub-case (R21-R1, naming note) but hides no behaviour change. No product defect found.

findings.evidence: The second loop of the test runs the repeating edit list (4 samples of 20 units, edits [(40,0),(40,0)], request (0,4) presents samples 0,1,0,1, the packet loop delivers samples 0 and 1 once each, so the receipt is Partial from the packets: 2 units, end 40 units) with two plans: Plan::Works (2 pictures, end 40 units = the packet end) and Plan::DropPicture(1) (1 picture, end 20 units, NOT the packet end). The second row is a decoder-dropped Partial, the subject of the other new test; it is the row the lane's red proof reports failing (left 16934400000 = 40 x 423360000, right 8467200000 = 20 x 423360000). So the name is wider than the content, but the failure is not a behaviour change of a fully delivered decode: every fully delivered row (:1290-1312: (0,3) Preview and Export, (pts[1],2) pre-roll, (pts[2],1) Preview and Export, both fixtures; :1319 with :1339-1342 the packet-short Works case) asserts receipt.actual == the packet receipt's actual and holds on both trees. By code: the Partial branch is entered only when delivered < req.count (video.rs:541); a complete decode skips it. When the packets themselves fall short and every non-preroll packet yields a picture, Forward::accept computes pts + duration from the same PacketMeta the packet loop used for its chunk (video.rs:400-407, :384-385; Forward skips preroll pictures :343-345 as the loop skips preroll chunks isobmff.rs:2139), takes the max as the loop does (isobmff.rs:2145) and clamps to the start as the loop's initial delivered_end does (video.rs:559 vs isobmff.rs:2104): the value is identical.
findings.repair_direction: Optional: move the DropPicture(1) row of the repeating-edit-list loop into partial_video_receipt_ends_at_the_last_delivered_picture (it is a decoder-drop over a packet-short range) or rename the test (for example fully_delivered_video_receipt_keeps_the_packet_end_and_a_drop_shortens_it); keep the DESCRIPTOR export.rule/export.tests citations in step.

In every new case the max of the delivered ends therefore equals the end of the last arrival, so a mutant `Some(end)` (last arrival instead of max) and a decoder that releases its tail in finish() are not exercised. By code both are handled: max is order-independent, and Forward::accept also runs from session.finish() (video.rs:534-536), before the receipt is patched (:541). lanes.recommendation_note: PLR-063 is fixed by code reading: the per-stack ceiling now cuts only switched-off instances of a visible stack with counted instances (typed Transformed loss), a stack with no counted instances past the ceiling is still not mapped, the counted bound of 64 still cuts. Dropped instances are not charged to the 4096 uncounted bound, the record never exceeds Folio's 1024 and the node need stays <= max_layers + 8192. One decision point for the lead (R21-S1: ALL switched-off instances of an over-ceiling stack are dropped, not only the excess), documented and consistent with R10; no product defect.

findings.severity: CONFIRMED (design as documented; lead decision point, not a defect)
findings.file_line: src/effects.rs:613-614 (switched-off kept while kept-off < 1024), :638-646 (over_stack -> retain enabled); tests/effects_budget.rs:867-887
findings.evidence: Answer to 'are off instances under the ceiling still kept': a stack at or under the ceiling keeps every switched-off instance (rows 1+1023 and 64+960 -> Kept(1024), effects_budget.rs:886-888; Whole when !over_stack). In a visible stack over the ceiling, the scan keeps up to 1024 switched-off instances and then `effects.retain(|e| e.enabled)` (:645) removes ALL of them, the ones that would have fitted included: the record holds the counted instances only (Fate::CountedOnlyStack(1) for 1 live + 1024 off). This is the lane's stated choice (notes.design 'choice', notes.not_done), the DESCRIPTOR clause ('a_stack_with_counted_instances_keeps_all_of_them_and_drops_its_switched_off_ones'), the effects.rs and proposal.rs docs, and the shape of the R10 lead decision 2026-10-11T15:43:55Z for the uncounted bound ('a visible stack keeps its live instances and drops its switched-off instances'). The dispatch phrase 'off instances over the ceiling dropped' can be read as 'only the excess'. Rendered output is the same either way (a switched-off instance renders nothing) and the lfx2 block stays byte-exact in the file (asserted :905-909). Keeping a prefix would charge that prefix to the 4096 uncounted bound; the second half of the test (:913-928, five such stacks leave the whole 4096 to hidden stacks) depends on 'none kept'.
findings.repair_direction: None for the code. Lead: confirm 'all switched-off instances of an over-ceiling visible stack' as the rule (or order a prefix variant, which must charge the kept prefix to the uncounted bound and use the existing CountedOnly fallback when it does not fit).

findings.evidence: Answer to 'is a typed loss emitted for every dropped instance': one Transformed entry per stack, effects_unrendered_dropped_over_stack_ceiling at layer[i]/tagged/lfx2(layer_id=...), with no count of the dropped instances; the same one-entry-per-stack convention as R10's effects_unrendered_dropped_over_document_budget. Every path that drops is covered: Fit::CountedOnlyOverStack is produced only when over_stack (effects.rs:647-650) and always maps to the entry; a stack with no counted instances over the ceiling is Err(effects_over_budget) (:640-641, or the early return :618-622), which is_budget_reason routes to tally.refused plus one Unsupported entry (proposal.rs:596-599). Test fate() (effects_budget.rs:420-445) asserts exactly one budget entry per layer with the expected code.

Instances that end up outside the record (switched-off ones past the ceiling, which are still mapped 'for their notes', and the kept ones removed by retain) still contribute their map_effect notes (for example an Unsupported contour note, :421-422); Builder::notes appends them without de-duplication. The loss report therefore lists per-instance Unsupported entries for instances the record does not hold. Over-reporting (safe direction), the same pattern as R10's CountedOnly retain, bounded by the descriptor reader caps (descriptor.rs:19, :21: 512 items per container, 8192 per descriptor). Before ceb9d33 an over-ceiling stack returned Err and its notes were discarded.
